newsitem.title: SPAIN: Heavy diet of purchases eats into Santander profit.
newsitem.headline: Heavy diet of purchases eats into Santander profit.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Monday that excluding the amortisation of goodwill from recent purchases, net attributable nine-months profit would have risen by 16.2 percent instead of by just 13.2 percent.
Santander, which amortises using a straight line method over 10 years, reported nine-month attributable profits of 71.78 billion pesetas, up 13.22 percent over the year-ago period.
Without amortisation, the bank said profits would have been 85.92 billion pesetas.
In the third quarter, the bank had amortisation of 5.17 billion pesetas, roughly half of which stemmed from the 1994 purchase of Banesto while the other half stemmed from purchases in Latin America.
Last week, Santander said it would take control of Mexico's Grupo Financiero Invermexico, which owns Banco Mexicano and Invermexico Casa de Bolsa.

The previously announced merger of Banco Santander Chile with Banco Osorno y La Union took effect on July 1. In Europe, Santander agreed at the beginning of July to buy up to 10 percent of Hungarian bank Inter Europa Bank for $6 million.
